title: A neural quantum state variational Monte Carlo study of Aharonov-Casher bands
summary: Neural variational Monte Carlo wave functions, benchmarked against multiband exact diagonalization on small systems, were used to map phases in the Aharonov–Casher continuum model up to 36 electrons. At filling 2/3 the calculations identified an incommensurate electron Wigner crystal and a triangular hole-crystal phase; the study also estimated a uniform-field Jain-state freezing threshold. This is theoretical and model-specific, with no direct experimental confirmation. This concerns the Aharonov–Casher model and is distinct from the active artificial-graphene paired-Wigner-crystal result.
ai_technology: Neural-network-based variational Monte Carlo wave functions (a flux-attachment-informed ansatz and a Slater–Jastrow ansatz) represented competing correlated ground states, enabling multiband calculations beyond exact-diagonalization sizes.
organization: University of California, Berkeley; University of Cambridge

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version and date verified from primary record.

evidence.tested: Two neural variational wavefunctions were compared against multiband exact diagonalization on small systems; phase characterization used charge density, structure factors, pair correlations, Chern number and flux-pumping checks.
evidence.unknown: Predictions are specific to the continuum model and finite simulated systems; no direct experimental confirmation. Related active record 2026-04-study-10-21203-rs-3-rs-9316409-v1 concerns a distinct artificial-graphene paired crystal.
